column13: Explanation — Machzor gadol — the twenty-eight-year solar cycle Machzor gadol is the 28-year cycle obtained from Shmuel’s 365¼-day year. Relative to a seven-day week, the quarter-day annual excess yields the original weekday-and-hour alignment again after twenty-eight years. Birkat HaChamah, the Blessing of the Sun, is recited on the morning associated with that modeled return every twenty-eight years. This is a calendar calculation, not a claim that the physical sun returns to exactly the same astronomical coordinates only every twenty-eight years.

column11: Genesis 15:6: ‘And he put his trust in GOD, who reckoned it to his merit.’ Context and connection to Machshavot Charutz: In Machshavot Charutz 19, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Genesis 15:6) to illuminate his exposition here (“and Avraham Avinu was the beginning of faith: "And he believed in Hashem, and He counted it to him for righteousness" (Bereishis 15:6); this being the foundation of building the Israelite nation...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the supernal levels of Thought (Machshavah), the rectification of human desire and intellect, and the inner light of the Oral Torah developed in Machshavot Charutz.
column13: And already at the start of Sefer HaChinnukh, he counted the mitzvah of faith in God among the continual commandments whose obligation is perpetual, yet his intention is that there is not a single instant wherein one is permitted to cease believing in the Blessed Name, God forbid, rather than demanding unbroken active contemplation of faith; however, to attain the perfection of faith, constant contemplation and internal clarification of its truth are essential.

column11: Bereshit Rabbah 42:8: ‘“The refugee came and told Abram the Hebrew, and he was dwelling in the plains of Mamre the Emorite, brother of Eshkol and brother of Aner, and they were allies of Abram” (Genesis 14:13). “The refugee came” – Reish Lakish in the name of bar Kappara: This is Og; he is the “refugee.” Why is he called Og? Because he came and found Abram sitting and engaging in the mitzva of baking [unleavened] loaves [ugot] [for Passover]. His intentions [in informing Abraham] were not to act for the sake of Heaven. Rather, he said: ‘This Abraham is a zealot. If I say to him now: Your nephew has been taken captive, he will go out to war and be killed, and I will take his wife Sarai.’ The Holy One blessed be He said to him: ‘By your life, you will receive reward for your strides that you walked [to travel to Abraham], in that you will live long in the world.…’ Context and connection to Machshavot Charutz: In Machshavot Charutz 19, Rav Tzadok cites this midrashic exposition (Bereshit Rabbah 42:8) to illuminate his exposition here (“and because he had not yet been refined from the status of a proselyte to be accounted as a native-born Israelite and designated "the Ezrachite" (Bereishis Rabbah 42:8); his faith had not yet...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the supernal levels of Thought (Machshavah), the rectification of human desire and intellect, and the inner light of the Oral Torah developed in Machshavot Charutz.
column13: Now, the physical universe and the corporeal body are material and destined for dissolution, including the physical heavens and earth (Bereishit Rabbah 42); whereas Time (Shanah / the order of seasons) has no physical tangibility. Therefore our Sages taught in Bereishit Rabbah that a sequence of times existed prior to Creation, and as stated: the Torah preceded the world by two thousand years, which constitutes a non-physical temporal order.
